text:
Ivy: quick post-release triage. Two signals: (1) customers reporting intermittent tail latency on long chat sessions, (2) PMs collecting ~10 low-effort UX follow-ons from pilots. do we prioritize SLA-impacting fixes first or batch polish into a follow-up minor?

Max: need numbers. if tail latency affects SLAs or billing pipelines -> hotfix first. can you paste metrics?

Ivy: metrics: customer Y p99 for 12k-token sessions spiked from ~650ms -> ~1.2s under sustained load; error rate small but retries up. UX list: copy tweaks, onboarding microflow reorder, small modal accessibility label. most are low-effort 1-2 dev-hours.

Harper: bugs-first. runtime work is noisy — prefer to isolate a focused perf squad. polish can be owned asynchronously by product/design so we don't block runtime.

Chris: agree. quick mitigation may be a pacing guard + K/V cache aggressive reclaim. estimate: mitigation + canary = 3 engineer-days. full runtime fix ~7 engineer-days. polish work = 2 engineers part-time across week.

Ivy: Ops flagged we have limited canary nodes this week. ops-bot can you check reservations?

ops-bot: Reservation check: available canary pools this week: pool-a (2 GPUs, 6h), pool-b (4 GPUs, 12h). Please specify. :white_check_mark:

Max: proposal: 7-day micro-cycle. Day 0: triage + owner assignment. Day 1-3: mitigation + canary. Day 4-6: full runtime patch if mitigation insufficient. Day 7: roll and quick polish sweep to close low-effort items. Freeze serving-runtime merges except hotfixes for the cycle.

Harper: acceptance criteria for rollout: p99 <=700ms for 12k token in staging under perf harness OR retries <=0.3% for 6h steady. polish acceptance: close >=70% of low-effort UX items or mark them scheduled with owners.

Chris: canary plan below — pinning to #eng-oncall:
```
canary plan v1
1. deploy pacing_guard=true on pool-b canary nodes
2. route 3% production traffic for 2h
3. run load scenario: ./perf/long_chat --tokens 12000 --qps 30 --duration 120
4. collect metrics: p99_latency, retry_rate, kv_cache_pressure
5. if p99 improves to <=700ms for 90m, expand to 20% for 3h then roll
```

ops-bot: Canary created: canary-2401 on pool-b. Alerts forwarded to #eng-oncall and #product.

Ivy: freeze note: block merges touching serving-runtime and routing. allow docs, examples, and UI polish PRs (label:postlaunch-polish) to proceed.

Max: QA plan: two monitoring windows during canary (start + mid-run) and a 30m smoke after roll. Chris, can you coordinate QA?

Chris: will allocate QA slots and post schedule. also will hook up synthetic checks to alert if retries >0.5%.

Harper: communication: notify affected pilots with a short note: "We're deploying a targeted mitigation for long-session tail latency; we expect minimal impact and will follow up with runtime improvements next week." include acceptance criteria and timeline.

Ivy: decision: spin up two squads — perf-squad (Max lead) and polish-surge (Harper lead, asynchronous). ops to run canary on pool-b. freeze runtime merges. I'll notify sales/support and update the roadmap card with acceptance criteria.

Max: I'll open the perf ticket with owners and link this thread. tagging all runtime PRs with label:hotfix.

Harper: I'll split the UX list into low/med/high and take the low ones in this cycle. posting PR checklist for quick reviews now.

ops-bot: Canary status: scheduled window tomorrow 09:00-21:00 UTC. Reservation pool-b confirmed. :thumbsup:

Chris: noted. QA ready for 09:30 UTC. check-in tomorrow 08:45 to confirm canary ramp.

Ivy: thanks everyone. if canary fails, fallback is revert or enable conservative pacing guard and widen the mitigation. postmortem trigger if p99 >1s or retries >1% for >4h. next check-in 08:45 UTC. :rocket:
